verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched with a browser UA, 200. The heading appears verbatim (with a period) in the Basic-AI-vs-Muse comparison strip, paired with 'Muse will write anything - no filters.' The page's term is 'Basic AI', exemplified in the adjacent column by a named ChatGPT refusal, which carries the claim's 'general-purpose models' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: offer both sides of an argument in a single response
verdicts.note: Raw Guardian page, 200; byline 'Alex Hern', dateline 'Tue 16 Apr 2024'. The quoted string appears verbatim inside the paragraph opening 'Other tells are less noticeable in isolation', which lists it with an aversion to single-sentence replies and flawless spelling as 'robotic writing'. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Its endless "not thing x, but thing y" parallelisms
verdicts.note: Raw tumblr page, 200. In the 'Background: R1' section the post introduces 'a selection from Coagulopath's 7-point description of R1's style', and quoted point 7 is headed 'repetitive writing' and includes the phrase verbatim alongside the italicised-last-word habit. Attribution, section and point number all match.

verdicts.trueWording: AI uses it constantly, reflexively, in situations where it adds nothing
verdicts.note: Raw ignorance.ai page, 200; byline 'Charlie Guo', dated 'Oct 22, 2025'. Under the heading 'Parallelism (It's Not X, It's Y)' the page first concedes it is 'a perfectly legitimate rhetorical device', then the quoted sentence follows (page prefixes 'But'). Both limbs of the claim supported.

verdicts.trueWording: tidy, explicit, causally legible, emotionally annotated, and thematically over-secured
verdicts.note: Raw dramatica.com page, 200; byline 'The Dramatica Co.', dated May 29, 2026. In the section 'The Cluster Is the Warning' the page frames the danger as AI producing a vast amount of competent fiction sharing one underlying shape, then gives the quoted five-term list verbatim. Section name and every limb match.

Raw arXiv HTML for 2604.03136v6, 200. The string appears verbatim in section 4.1 ('What core narrative choices separate human from AI writing?'), in the paragraph headed 'Human authors subvert linearity.' The sentence reads 'AI stories exhibit tighter causal chains, more protagonist-driven resolutions (69% vs. 46%)', fixing 69% to AI and 46% to human as the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: Gemini produces the tidiest endings, extended denouements
verdicts.note: Raw arXiv HTML for 2604.03136v6, 200. The string appears verbatim in section 5, 'Pinpointing each source's writing style', in the paragraph headed 'Gemini, DeepSeek, and Kimi are triplets'. The paper continues 'and the bleakest settings (88% tagged bleak and oppressive)', which the claim does not assert. Per-model fingerprint framing is the paper's own.

verdicts.trueWording: Many LLM-generated Wikipedia articles include a "Challenges" section
verdicts.note: Raw Wikipedia page fetched 2026-09-07, 200. Quote verbatim in the section 'Outline-like conclusions about challenges and future prospects'. The page gives the formula (opens 'Despite its [positive/promotional words]...'; 'usually appear at the end of articles with a rigid outline structure'), supporting 'rigid formula'. Note the page's ending is a disjunction: 'ends with either a vaguely positive assessment... or speculation about how ongoing or potential initiatives could benefit the subject' - the claim names the first disjunct only, which the page does support.

Raw Wikipedia page, 200. In section 'Negative parallelisms', subsection 'Not just X, but also Y', the page reads 'It is common for LLMs to use parallel constructions involving "not", "but", or "however" such as "Not only ... but ... " or "It is not just ..., it's ..."' - the supplied quote is verbatim and both named example forms match the claim exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: a construction particularly common in Grok output
verdicts.note: Raw Wikipedia page, 200. The claim IS supported, but not by the supplied quote. The support is in section 'Negative parallelisms', subsection 'X rather than Y': 'This pattern may also be reversed, a construction particularly common in Grok output.' The supplied quote 'Grok output is particularly idiosyncratic' does appear verbatim, but in the AI-vocabulary section about overused words (causal, empirical, correlate, underscore) - a different finding. Graded SUBSTANCE rather than VERBATIM because the quotation does not evidence the sentence it is attached to; any downstream use must cite the 'X rather than Y' sentence, not this one.

verdicts.trueWording: The obituaries are detached and nearly identical to one another
verdicts.note: Raw Verge page, 200; byline Mia Sato, 'Feb 12, 2024'. Quote verbatim; the page continues 'with a few words moved around and repeating inaccurate details, like where Mazur lived', carrying the reordered-words limb. The dozen-plus limb rests on 'The Verge identified over a dozen websites that published articles about Mazur's death' plus 'numerous bogus obituaries about Mazur'; Beth Mazur is the one dead woman. The claim's 'differing only by' is marginally tighter than the page, which also cites repeated inaccuracies.

verdicts.trueWording: written with a nondescript gravitas, using unnatural phrasing
verdicts.note: Raw Verge page, 200. Verbatim in the section on The Thaiger: 'The obituary articles are written with a nondescript gravitas, using unnatural phrasing like...'. Both limbs (nondescript gravitas; built out of unnatural phrasing) are the page's own construction.

verdicts.trueWording: the "indelible mark" a person has left, or their "untimely demise"
verdicts.note: Raw Verge page, 200. The two phrases appear verbatim (with curly quotation marks in the source) in the same Thaiger sentence, introduced by 'using unnatural phrasing like', which is exactly the relation the claim asserts.

verdicts.trueWording: but without any actual detail about their life
verdicts.note: Raw Verge page, 200. Verbatim clause closing the same Thaiger sentence, so the contrast the claim draws (elevated phrasing yet no detail about the dead person) is the page's own sentence structure. The next sentence reinforces it: the articles 'lack quotes from family or friends of the deceased and do not cite outside reporting.'

verdicts.trueWording: sometimes using identical vague phrases about the deceased
verdicts.note: Raw Verge page, 200. Verbatim in the Thaiger section: 'The stories follow a similar structure, sometimes using identical vague phrases about the deceased.' The 'one site' is named as The Thaiger and the deceased are described as different individuals (illness deaths, student suicides, minors in car accidents), supporting the 'different deceased people' limb.
